رِتَاقٌ [A garment composed of] two pieces of cloth sewed together (يُرْتَقَانِ) by their borders. (Lth, S, K.) Hence the saying of a rájiz, “جَارِيَ بَيْضَآءُ فِى رِتَاقِ
تُدِيرُ طَرْفًا أَكْحَلَ المَآقِى
” [A fair girl in a رتاق, turning about eyes black in the inner angles.] (Lth, S. *)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
